title: The Lament of Likai (Ka Likai)
cultural_context: The tragic folk ballad of Ka Likai, the grieving mother whose sorrow gave name to the magnificent Nohkalikai Falls.
lyrics_khasi:
Ha kliar u riat ba jrong,
Ka Likai ka la ieng,
Dohnud ba la pait dor-dor
Kam don shuh ban kynroi;
La duh i khun ba ieit,
Iba kum u syntiew phuh,
Ka pyrthei ka la dum,
Khlem jingshai shuh ban meh.

Sha thwai ba jylliew ka kshaid
Ka la pashat la ka met,
Ka um ka la shim ia ka
Ha pneh ba jar-jar;
Naduh kato ka sngi
Ka kshaid ka la ioh kyrteng,
Nohkalikai ba sawa
Ka sur pangnud jong ka kmie.
lyrics_english:
Upon the rim of the towering precipice,
Likai stood motionless,
Her heart shattered in pieces
Past all human consolation;
Lost was her darling infant child,
Fair as a fresh-blown flower,
The entire world grew pitch dark,
With no remaining light to glow.

Into the deep pool of the gorge
She plunged from the cliff,
The waters embraced her gently
In tranquil peace forever;
From that fateful day onward
The roaring cascade took her name:
Nohkalikai, echoing forever
The weeping sorrow of a mother's heart.
